done.why: I typed a 31st line (go east, heading back toward the reservoir) and was told I'd used all 30 turns the session allows. I was still mildly interested, not bored yet, but I'd also only found one real sign that this was a changed version of the game I half-recognised.

about: A white house in a field with a trap door under the rug, leading into caves full of trolls and treasure. You're meant to collect treasures and put them in a trophy case that 'expects to be filled'. This version seems altered somewhere underground — the Round Room has cave-ins blocking passages, and the trap door got barred behind me — but in 30 turns I didn't get far enough to see what the changes really amount to.

moments.note: The trophy case 'has the patient air of something that expects to be filled' — a nice line that told me what the game wants from me without a tutorial.
Trap door slammed and someone barred it behind me. Slightly creepy; also told me I couldn't just go back up.
Missed the troll and got dropped to my knees; the fight stretched across five turns for a guy in a hurry.
Beheaded the troll, he dissolved into black fog. Satisfying after the slog.
Round Room says several passages are blocked by cave-ins — first sign this isn't quite the place I remembered.
'Bar bar ...' — the room swallowing my command was baffling for a second before I twigged it was echoing.
Saying 'echo' worked and I got the platinum bar. Felt clever.
Walked west along the stream into a dead end, then got cut off by the turn cap right as I turned around.

wished: I wished I could find out what the cave-ins in the Round Room were about — which passages were blocked and whether I could clear them.
I wished I'd had enough turns to get back to the trophy case and actually put the platinum bar in it, since the case practically asked for it.
I wished the troll fight had been shorter; five turns of swinging at one guy is a lot when you've only got a few minutes.
I wished I knew who barred the trap door behind me.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: Gave the whole game a goal in one sentence, and it was the first thing that read as new rather than familiar.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: Made the house feel occupied by something and cut off my retreat — raised the stakes.

lines.line: It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head.
lines.why: The payoff for a frustrating fight; funny and final.

lines.line: Several of them have unfortunately been blocked by cave-ins.
lines.why: The clearest sign that this version differs from the one I vaguely knew; it made me want to see which routes were gone.
Confusing, then a puzzle clue — the room was mocking me and I had to figure out why.

fun.why: Beheading the troll and solving the echo room were genuinely fun; the fight itself dragged and the stream dead-end wasted my last turns.

engagement.why: The barred trap door and the cave-ins hooked me a little, but most of the half hour was walking familiar rooms. I wasn't bored when the cap hit, but I wasn't gripped either.

difficulty.why: Nothing stopped me outright. The troll fight was a dice-roll grind and the echo room needed one guess, which I got. Felt about right for a casual player.

interestingness.why: The trophy case line, the barred door, and the cave-ins all hinted at a changed world, but I only saw hints — I never reached whatever the real change is.

prose.why: Mostly brisk and clear, with a couple of standout lines (the trophy case, the troll's end). The echo gag landed. Room descriptions are terse but never confusing.
